questions.question: Converting "studies", "studying" and "studied" to "studi" by chopping suffixes is:
questions.explanation: Stemming applies crude suffix rules and may produce non-words. Lemmatization would give "study".

questions.question: Which step uses a vocabulary and part of speech to map "better" to "good"?
questions.explanation: Lemmatization returns the dictionary form (lemma) and needs the word's POS.

questions.question: A bag-of-words representation loses:
questions.explanation: BoW keeps counts but discards order and grammar: "dog bites man" = "man bites dog".

questions.question: A corpus has 1,000 documents and a term occurs in 100 of them. Using log base 10, its IDF is:
A term appears in every document of the corpus. Its TF-IDF weight in any document is:
questions.explanation: IDF = log(N/N) = log 1 = 0, so TF × IDF = 0.

questions.question: A term appears 3 times in a 60-word document; its IDF (log₁₀) is 2. TF-IDF = ?
Why are one-hot vectors poor at capturing meaning?
options: Every pair of distinct words is equally dissimilar (orthogonal)
questions.explanation: The dot product of any two different one-hot vectors is 0, so "cat" is as far from "dog" as from "car".

questions.question: Word2Vec CBOW is trained to:
options: Predict context words from the centre word
Predict the centre word from its context
questions.explanation: CBOW: context → word. Skip-gram: word → context.

questions.question: Which Word2Vec variant generally works better for rare words?
questions.explanation: Skip-gram makes several training examples per occurrence of a word, so rare words get more updates.

questions.question: GloVe embeddings are built mainly from:
questions.explanation: GloVe = Global Vectors: factorises a co-occurrence matrix. FastText uses character n-grams.

questions.question: Which embedding can build a vector for a word never seen in training, using its character n-grams?
questions.explanation: FastText represents a word as a bag of character n-grams, so new words get vectors from their pieces.

questions.question: The word "bank" gets the same vector in "river bank" and "bank loan" with:
questions.explanation: Word2Vec, GloVe and FastText are static. BERT, ELMo and GPT give contextual embeddings.

questions.question: Vectors a = (1, 0, 1) and b = (1, 1, 0). Cosine similarity = ?
"king − man + woman ≈ queen" shows that embeddings:
options: Encode semantic relations as vector directions
questions.explanation: Consistent offsets between word vectors capture relations like gender.

questions.question: Identifying "Infosys" as an ORGANISATION and "Bengaluru" as a LOCATION is:
questions.explanation: NER labels spans with entity types (person, organisation, location, date…).

questions.question: Which are standard text-preprocessing steps? (select all)
questions.explanation: Backpropagation is how networks are trained, not preprocessing.

questions.question: Subword tokenizers such as BPE and WordPiece mainly solve:
questions.explanation: Unknown words are split into known subword pieces, e.g. "unhappiness" → un + happi + ness.

questions.question: A bigram model of "I love NLP" considers which pairs?
questions.explanation: Bigrams are consecutive 2-word sequences.

questions.question: The distributional hypothesis states that:
options: Words appearing in similar contexts have similar meanings
questions.explanation: "You shall know a word by the company it keeps" (Firth) — the basis of embeddings.

questions.question: A spam classifier that predicts 100 emails as spam, of which 80 are truly spam, has precision:
questions.explanation: Precision = TP / predicted positive = 80/100.

questions.question: Naive Bayes for text classification assumes that:
options: Words are conditionally independent given the class
questions.explanation: The "naive" independence assumption makes it fast and a strong baseline.

questions.question: Vocabulary size is 50,000. A one-hot vector for a word has length:
questions.explanation: One position per vocabulary word.

questions.question: Which is an example of natural language generation (NLG) rather than understanding?
options: Writing a product description from bullet points
questions.explanation: NLG produces text; the others classify or label it.

questions.question: Negative sampling in Word2Vec is used to:
options: Make training efficient by updating only a few wrong words per step
questions.explanation: Instead of a softmax over the whole vocabulary, a few random negative words are contrasted with the true one.
